page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. Powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor, it features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 1890 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in large-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores. Multi-core processing benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, rank in the top 25%, as do software compilation tasks using Clang. Database performance is a notable strength, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top 10% and Redis SET operations demonstrating strong throughput. However, single-core performance and large-model LLM inference tasks remain average or poor, highlighting a tradeoff where parallelized workloads are favored over single-threaded execution.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32plds_v6 offers a resource-dense compute profile by pairing a high number of dedicated ARM cores with a streamlined memory footprint. This makes it highly suitable for scale-out workloads that require substantial processing power without the overhead of excess RAM. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, database operations, and data compression tasks.
